Equivalent: round(lat, 2) vs round(lat, 3). _LAT_FIT values have at most one decimal place, so the extra precision changes nothing.
Equivalent: round(ctx, 2) vs round(ctx, 3). _context_fit only ever returns 0.6, 0.7 or 1.0, so rounding to 2 vs 3 places is identical.
Equivalent: round(adj, 2) vs round(adj, 3). _use_case_adjust only produces values with at most two decimals (0.0, +/-0.05, +/-0.10, -0.05), so the third place is always zero.

agentrouter.hosts.x_execution_route_bloc: Equivalent: mutates the dead 'unknown' fallback in `status.availability if status else 'unknown'`. The early guard requires execution_targets, so resolve_execution_route always returns a non-None status here; the else branch is unreachable.
Equivalent: uppercases the dead 'unknown' fallback string. status is always non-None once the execution_targets guard passes, so this else branch never executes.
Equivalent: mutates the dead 'no execution target' fallback in `status.reason if status else ...`. status is guaranteed non-None after the execution_targets guard; the else branch is unreachable.
Equivalent: uppercases the dead 'no execution target' fallback string. Unreachable because status is always non-None when the model has execution targets.
agentrouter.hosts.x_resolve_execution_ro: Equivalent: zip(strict=False) vs strict=True. statuses is derived per-target from execution_targets so the two iterables are always equal length; no behavioural difference.
Equivalent: zip(strict=None) vs strict=True. statuses is built one-per-target from the same execution_targets list, so lengths are always equal and strict has no observable effect.
Equivalent: zip(strict removed) vs strict=True. statuses length always equals execution_targets length, so strict never triggers; behaviour identical.

The value is used only as `attrs & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT` (0x400); both 0 and 1 have no bits in common with 0x400, so the result is False either way. agentrouter.plugins.x__remove_owned_empt: Equivalent at this call site: mutates the `label` argument of the `_directory_lstat(staged, ...)` call inside the `except (PluginError, OSError)` recovery block of `_remove_owned_empty_directory`. `label` is used in exactly two places in `_directory_lstat` -- the messages of the "disappeared during the operation" and "is not a safe directory" PluginErrors -- and that call is wrapped in `try: ... except PluginError: pass`, so both messages are discarded without being read, logged or re-raised. No caller can observe the string. The same mutation on the non-recovery `_directory_lstat` calls, whose PluginError does propagate, IS killed by tests in tests/test_plugins_decisions.py that assert the message prefix. This variant passes None as the label.
